I have followed ISRG since 2003 when it was brought to the investing club I had just joined. I tried to analyze ISRG with the BetterInvesting SSG methodology that I had been introduced to and I could not get it in the buy zone. Wiser heads in the club prevailed and we started a position at around $48 a share and continued to add to the position. In 2005 ISRG was trading at over $200 a share and I was getting nervous. I convinced the club to place a trailing stop on ISRG. The price continued to increase and reached $393 a share. Then ISRG stock price started to drop and it got as low as $200 a share. Our trailing stop worked like a charm and we were sold out of the club position at just above $360 a share. I tried to convince the club to reinvest in ISRG at $200 a share; they decided not to, but I did. I describe it as riding the lightning. That pattern aligns with a recurring usage model, where installed robots create ongoing demand for proprietary tools and support.

Alongside that qualitative angle, Intuitive Surgical’s own fundamentals show earnings growth of 17.5% per year over the past 5 years and current annual revenue of about $11.6b with net income of roughly $3.0b. Forecasts in the dataset point to earnings expected to grow 15.18% per year and revenue projected to increase around 11% annually, which supports the idea of a profitable, growing franchise rather than a purely speculative robotics play.
